intent: Lay out one form control together with its label, its description and its validation message.
typical_uses: A labelled text entry with helper text below it
A switch or checkbox with its caption and description beside it, in the horizontal orientation

dont_use_when.situation: A caption for a control outside any Field composition
Several related fields presented under one shared title
A multi-step form answered one question at a time

mounted_in.container: the consuming application's own form or section element
mounted_in.note: A Field needs no FieldGroup or FieldSet around it; only the responsive orientation depends on a FieldGroup ancestor.

invariants.text: Field always renders a div with role="group" and a data-orientation attribute carrying the orientation, "vertical" when none is given.

Field and its parts create no ids and no associations: FieldLabel's htmlFor, the control's id and the control's aria-describedby pointing at a FieldDescription or FieldError id are all set by the consumer.

data-invalid="true" on Field sets its text color to --danger, which FieldLabel, FieldTitle and every other descendant that declares no color of its own inherit. It sets nothing on the control: the control's own aria-invalid is set separately.
data-disabled="true" on Field dims every FieldLabel and FieldTitle inside it to the disabled opacity. It does not disable the control; the control's own disabled prop does that.

vertical stacks the direct children in a column at full width; horizontal lays them in a row centered on the cross axis, a direct FieldLabel child growing to fill the row, and switches to top alignment when a direct child is a FieldContent; responsive stays stacked until the nearest FieldGroup ancestor is at least 28rem wide and then lays out as horizontal does. It measures that FieldGroup, not the viewport, and with no FieldGroup ancestor it stays stacked.

anti_patterns.dont: Put two controls in one Field
anti_patterns.do_instead: Give each control its own Field, and group the Fields with FieldGroup or FieldSet

anti_patterns.dont: Name the group with a label pointing at the Field
anti_patterns.do_instead: Point FieldLabel's htmlFor at the control's id; a `<label for>` cannot name the Field's div, which is not a labelable element

a11y.by: field.test.tsx asserts role="group" on the rendered Field, and that getByLabelText finds the Input whose id a FieldLabel's htmlFor names

good.title: A text field wired by hand to its label and description
good.code:
<Field>
  <FieldLabel htmlFor="email">Email</FieldLabel>
  <Input id="email" type="email" aria-describedby="email-desc" />
  <FieldDescription id="email-desc">We only use it for the invoice.</FieldDescription>
</Field>

good.title: An invalid field showing a validation message
good.code:
<Field data-invalid={Boolean(error)}>
  <FieldLabel htmlFor="slug">Slug</FieldLabel>
  <Input id="slug" aria-invalid={Boolean(error)} aria-describedby="slug-error" />
  <FieldError id="slug-error">{error}</FieldError>
</Field>

good.title: A switch with its label and description beside it
good.code:
<Field orientation="horizontal">
  <FieldContent>
    <FieldLabel htmlFor="updates">Product updates</FieldLabel>
    <FieldDescription>Release notes and roadmap changes.</FieldDescription>
  </FieldContent>
  <Switch id="updates" />
</Field>

bad.title: Expecting the label to find the control by itself
bad.why: Field wires nothing: with no htmlFor on FieldLabel and no id on the Input the caption names nothing and clicking it focuses nothing.

bad.title: A disabled prop on Field
bad.why: Field is a div and has no disabled prop: tsc refuses it, and at runtime the attribute reaches the div and does nothing. Set `disabled` on the control, and data-disabled on Field to dim its captions.

cannot_extract: default: prop "orientation" is read through `??` and also as its own value, so no one literal is its default - the contract states no default for it
